title: Naturality of projected ordinary evaluation under precomposition
statement: For X,U and arbitrary P,F, let C be the projected ordinary evaluation components of [def-pc-ordinary-evaluation-data]. Given integers p,q,qprime,n,m,r,s with p+q=n, p+qprime=m, r+qprime=0, s+q=0, s+n=r+m, maps f:P^r→P^s and a:D^q→D^qprime, and z an integer unit, assume a followed by the projection at (qprime,r,0) equals z times the projection at (q,s,0) followed by homObjMap(f,id). Then (id_F^p tensor a) followed by C(p,qprime,m,r) equals z times C(p,q,n,s) followed by homObjMap(f, the canonical transport F^(s+n)→F^(r+m)). This is purely evaluation naturality; a need not be a differential.

proof.text: Factor both nonzero components using [lem-pc-ordinary-evaluation-component-factorization]. Postcompose the projection hypothesis with the canonical degree-zero unit identification and use homObjMap functoriality. The private proved evaluation_precomposition and evaluation_naturality lemmas use tensorHomEquiv naturality from [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. The private proved evaluation_scaled lemma moves the integer unit scalar through tensorLeft and composition. Apply it to the two identified projections. Compose the canonical XIsoOfEq output transports to finish.

theorem ordinaryEvaluation_precomposition_naturality (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (P F : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ)
    (p q q' n m r s : ℤ) (hpq : p + q = n) (hpq' : p + q' = m)
    (hr : r + q' = 0) (hs : s + q = 0) (ht : s + n = r + m)
    (f : P.X r ⟶ P.X s)
    (a : (localEvaluationDual X U P).X q ⟶ (localEvaluationDual X U P).X q')
    (z : ℤˣ)
    (ha : a ≫ localEvaluationProjection X U P (localEvaluationUnit X U) q' r 0 hr =
      z • (localEvaluationProjection X U P (localEvaluationUnit X U) q s 0 hs ≫
        SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf.over U) f
          (𝟙 ((localEvaluationUnit X U).X 0)))) :
    (F.X p ◁ a) ≫ localEvaluationComponent X U P F p q' m r hpq' =
      z • (localEvaluationComponent X U P F p q n s hpq ≫
        SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf.over U) f (F.XIsoOfEq ht).hom)
